title: Claude Code Pricing: Which Claude Plan Do You Actually Need?
excerpt: Claude Code is not in the Free plan. Here is what Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise include, what each costs, and how to choose without overpaying.
seoTitle: Claude Code Pricing: Which Claude Plan Do You Need?
seoDescription: What Claude Code costs on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise, what each plan includes and how to pick the cheapest plan that fits your usage.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
A lower-priced alternative if you mostly want inline help in your editor.

content:
**Quick answer:** [Claude Code](/tools/claude-code) is not part of the Free plan. Most individuals should start on **Pro** ($17 a month billed annually, or $20 billed monthly) and only move to **Max** (from $100 a month) if they keep hitting usage limits. Teams use Team seats, and large organisations use Enterprise.

*Prices below were checked on Anthropic's pricing page on 16 October 2026. Plans, prices and usage limits can change, so confirm on the vendor page before you buy.*

## What Claude Code is

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool. According to its documentation it reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and connects to your development tools. You can use it from the terminal, from IDE extensions, from a desktop app and from the browser. Most of those surfaces need a Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account.

## The plans that include it

| Plan | Price | Claude Code | Who it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | No | Trying Claude chat |
| Pro | $17/month billed annually ($200 up front), or $20 monthly | Yes | Individual developers |
| Max | From $100/month | Yes | People who use Claude all day |
| Team, standard seat | $20/seat/month billed annually, or $25 monthly | All Claude features | Teams of 2 to 150 |
| Team, premium seat | $100/seat/month billed annually, or $125 monthly | Listed with Claude Code | Heavier users on a team |
| Enterprise | Seat price plus usage at API rates | Yes | Large organisations |

Prices exclude applicable tax, and Anthropic notes that usage limits apply on every plan.

## Pro or Max?

Pro is the plan Anthropic lists for everyday work. It includes Claude Code, more usage than Free, Claude in Chrome and Microsoft 365 connections.

Max is described as the plan for people who work with Claude all day. It includes everything in Pro and lets you choose **5x or 20x more usage than Pro**, along with higher output limits, early access to advanced features and priority access at high-traffic times. The Max tiers also list monthly API credits ($100 a month for Max 5x and $200 a month for Max 20x on the comparison table).

The practical rule: start on Pro. If you regularly run out of usage during your working day, the 5x tier of Max is the next step. Moving up before you have hit a limit just raises the bill.

## Team and Enterprise

Team plans are for 2 to 150 people. The standard seat includes all Claude features with more usage than Pro. The premium seat has 5x more usage than a standard seat and is the seat that lists Claude Code and Claude Cowork. Team adds central billing, single sign-on and admin controls for connectors.

Enterprise is priced as a seat fee plus usage at API rates (Anthropic shows US$20 per seat per month billed annually with a 20-seat minimum) and adds role-based access, SCIM, audit logs, a compliance API and custom data retention controls.

## Before you pay

- **Check billing terms.** The $17 Pro price is the annual rate; paying monthly is $20.
- **Remember the limits.** Every plan has usage limits, and the exact allowance is not a fixed number on the pricing page.
- **You will review code.** Claude Code edits files and runs commands in your repository, so treat its changes like a colleague's pull request.
- **Compare with an editor assistant.** If you mostly want suggestions inside your editor, a lower-priced option such as [GitHub Copilot](/tools/github-copilot) may be enough. See our [GitHub Copilot plans guide](/articles/github-copilot-plans-compared-free-pro-pro-plus-max).

Full details and our review are on the [Claude Code page](/tools/claude-code).

## Sources

- Anthropic pricing page (claude.com/pricing), checked 16 October 2026
- Claude Code documentation overview (docs.claude.com), checked 16 October 2026

title: DeepSeek API Pricing Explained: Flash vs Pro, Peak vs Off-Peak
excerpt: DeepSeek charges per million tokens, with different prices for cache hits, cache misses, output and time of day. Here is how to read it and estimate a bill.
seoTitle: DeepSeek API Pricing Explained: Flash vs Pro
seoDescription: How DeepSeek API pricing works: Flash and Pro rates, cache hit vs miss, peak and off-peak hours, with a worked example of what a job costs.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
Subscription-based alternative from Anthropic.

content:
**Quick answer:** [DeepSeek](/tools/deepseek) bills its API per 1 million tokens. Prices depend on the model (Flash or Pro), whether input tokens were a cache hit or miss, whether the tokens are input or output, and whether you call at peak or off-peak time. Off-peak rates are half of peak rates.

*Prices were taken from DeepSeek's API documentation on 16 October 2026. DeepSeek states that prices may vary and that it may adjust them, so check the page before you budget.*

## The two models

The pricing page lists two models:

- **deepseek-flash** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), which also supports vision.
- **deepseek-v4-pro** (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813), which does not support vision.

Both have a 1M-token context length and a maximum output of 384K, and both support JSON output, tool calls, a Responses API, an Anthropic-format API, and thinking and non-thinking modes. The older names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, but their requests are served by the V4.1-Flash model and billed at the Flash price.

## The prices (USD per 1M tokens)

| | Flash off-peak | Flash peak | Pro off-peak | Pro peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input, cache hit | $0.003 | $0.006 | $0.022 | $0.044 |
| Input, cache miss | $0.15 | $0.30 | $0.66 | $1.32 |
| Output | $0.60 | $1.20 | $1.98 | $3.96 |

## When is peak?

Peak hours are 01:00 to 04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full. If your jobs are not urgent, scheduling them off-peak halves the rate.

## A worked example

These are illustrations calculated from the listed prices, not DeepSeek figures. Suppose a job sends 1 million input tokens that are all cache misses and receives 200,000 output tokens.

- **Flash, off-peak:** 1 x $0.15 + 0.2 x $0.60 = **$0.27**
- **Flash, peak:** 1 x $0.30 + 0.2 x $1.20 = **$0.54**
- **Pro, off-peak:** 1 x $0.66 + 0.2 x $1.98 = **$1.056**
- **Pro, peak:** 1 x $1.32 + 0.2 x $3.96 = **$2.112**

If part of the input is served from cache, that part is billed at the much lower cache-hit price, so repeated prompts with a stable prefix cost less.

## Other charges and limits

- **Search and Fetch** are separate APIs billed per request: $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests each.
- **Billing** is deducted from your topped-up balance or granted balance, with the granted balance used first when both exist.
- **Concurrency limits** are listed as 2,500 for Flash and 500 for Pro.

## How to choose

Use Flash for cost-sensitive work and anything that needs images. Choose Pro when you want the larger model and can accept a price roughly three to four times the Flash rate. Because the API accepts OpenAI-format and Anthropic-format requests, you can point existing tools at it by changing the base URL.

Check DeepSeek's terms against your own data and compliance requirements before sending sensitive material. Our [DeepSeek page](/tools/deepseek) summarises the product, and for a subscription-based option compare [Claude](/tools/claude) and see [Claude Code pricing](/articles/claude-code-pricing-which-plan-do-you-need).

## Sources

- DeepSeek API docs, Models & Pricing (api-docs.deepseek.com), checked 16 October 2026

title: Supabase Pricing: Free Plan Limits and What Pro Adds
excerpt: What the Supabase Free plan actually includes, when the project pauses, what you get at $25 on Pro, and how compute credits work.
seoTitle: Supabase Pricing: Free Plan Limits and What Pro Adds
seoDescription: Supabase Free plan limits, the 1-week pause rule, what Pro at $25 adds, how compute credits work and when Team makes sense.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
A common hosting pairing for front ends built on Supabase.

content:
**Quick answer:** The Supabase Free plan costs $0 and includes 50,000 monthly active users, a 500 MB database and 1 GB of file storage, but projects pause after a week of inactivity and you are limited to 2 active projects. Pro starts at **$25 a month** and removes the pause, with more storage and daily backups.

*Checked on Supabase's pricing page on 16 October 2026. Prices and limits can change.*

## What the Free plan includes

According to the pricing page, Free is for passion projects and simple websites and includes:

- Unlimited API requests
- 50,000 monthly active users
- 500 MB database size, with shared CPU and 500 MB RAM
- 5 GB egress and 5 GB cached egress
- 1 GB file storage
- Community support

Two rules matter most: **free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity**, and you are limited to **2 active projects**. That makes Free fine for prototypes and learning, and risky for anything people depend on.

## What Pro adds

Pro is listed as "From $25 / month", with the first project included and additional projects from $10 a month. It is everything in Free plus:

- 100,000 monthly active users, then $0.00325 per additional user
- 8 GB disk per project, then $0.125 per GB
- 250 GB egress, then $0.09 per GB, and 250 GB cached egress, then $0.03 per GB
- 100 GB file storage, then $0.0213 per GB
- Email support
- Daily backups stored for 7 days and 7-day log retention

Pro also has a **spend cap on by default**, so costs stay under control until you choose to turn it off and pay for usage beyond the included quota.

## How compute credits work

Every project has its own dedicated Postgres instance, billed hourly. Paid plans include **$10 a month in compute credits**, enough to cover one Micro instance. Larger instances cost more:

| Size | Price per month | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Micro | $10 | 1 GB (shared compute) |
| Small | $15 | 2 GB (shared compute) |
| Medium | $60 | 4 GB (shared compute) |
| Large | $110 | 8 GB (2 dedicated vCPUs) |
| XL | $210 | 16 GB (4 dedicated vCPUs) |

The pricing page lists larger sizes up to 16XL as well. Credits offset any instance, so upgrading one project to Small means you pay the difference.

## Team and Enterprise

Team is listed from $599 a month and adds SOC2 and ISO 27001, project-scoped and read-only access, SSO for the dashboard, priority email support with SLAs, 14-day backups and 28-day log retention. HIPAA is available as a paid add-on. Enterprise is custom priced and adds technical account management, uptime SLAs and 24x7 support.

## Which plan to choose

1. **Experimenting or learning:** Free, accepting the pause rule.
2. **A live product with real users:** Pro, so projects do not pause and you get backups.
3. **Compliance or SSO requirements:** look at Team, or talk to Supabase about Enterprise.

Our [Supabase page](/tools/supabase) covers the product, and if you deploy the front end separately, see [Vercel pricing](/articles/vercel-pricing-hobby-vs-pro).

## Sources

- Supabase pricing page (supabase.com/pricing), checked 16 October 2026

title: GitHub Copilot Plans Compared: Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max
excerpt: GitHub Copilot now has four individual plans built around AI credits. This guide explains what each costs and which features need a paid plan.
seoTitle: GitHub Copilot Plans Compared: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max
seoDescription: GitHub Copilot Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max compared: monthly prices, how AI credits work, and which features need a paid plan.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
An agent-style alternative that works from the terminal.
An alternative with private and on-premise deployment.

content:
**Quick answer:** GitHub Copilot has four individual plans: **Free ($0), Pro ($10 a month), Pro+ ($39 a month) and Max ($100 a month)**. Free covers limited chat and agent use. Pull request reviews, assigning work to Copilot and the cloud agent need a paid plan.

*Checked on GitHub's Copilot plans page on 16 October 2026. Plans and credit allowances can change, and GitHub notes that flex allotments may change over time.*

## The four plans

| Plan | Price | Base credits | Flex allotment | Total credits shown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Limited chat and agent usage | Not included | Limited |
| Pro | $10/month | $10/month | $5/month | $15/month |
| Pro+ | $39/month | $39/month | $31/month | $70/month |
| Max | $100/month | $100/month | $100/month | $200/month |

## How credits work

GitHub explains that chat, agent mode, code review, the Copilot cloud agent, Copilot CLI and Copilot apps consume **GitHub AI Credits**. The Free plan supports the CLI and agent mode with limited usage. Paid plans include base credits plus a variable flex allotment, and Pro, Pro+ and Max can purchase additional credits.

The practical effect is that heavier use of agents and chat draws down your credits faster, so the plan you need depends on how much you ask Copilot to do rather than only on which features you want.

## What every plan includes

The comparison table marks these as included on Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max:

- Support in editors and IDEs, the CLI and on GitHub (github.com and GitHub Mobile)
- Agent mode in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode
- Integration with MCP servers
- Custom instructions and agents

## What needs a paid plan

The following are marked as not included on Free and included on Pro, Pro+ and Max:

- Assigning work to Copilot so it creates a pull request
- App modernization for Java and .NET
- Pull request reviews in GitHub and file diff reviews in code editors
- The Copilot cloud agent

## Which plan should you choose?

- **Trying it out or light use:** Free.
- **Regular daily use:** Pro is the lowest-priced paid plan and unlocks the paid features above.
- **Heavy agent use:** compare Pro+ and Max on how many credits you actually use before paying more.

If you prefer an agent that works across your whole repository from the terminal, compare [Claude Code](/tools/claude-code) and read our [Claude Code pricing guide](/articles/claude-code-pricing-which-plan-do-you-need). Teams that need private or on-premise deployment can also look at [Tabnine](/tools/tabnine).

Our [GitHub Copilot page](/tools/github-copilot) has the full review.

## Sources

- GitHub Copilot plans page (github.com/features/copilot/plans), checked 16 October 2026

title: Zendesk Pricing Explained: Support Team vs Suite Plans
excerpt: Zendesk lists four plans from $19 per agent a month. Here is what Support Team, Suite Team and Suite Professional include and who needs which.
seoTitle: Zendesk Pricing Explained: Support Team vs Suite
seoDescription: Zendesk plans compared: Support Team from $19, Suite Team $55, Suite Professional $115 per agent a month, plus what each tier includes.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
Another help desk with per-seat pricing and AI priced per outcome.
A help desk alternative to compare.

content:
**Quick answer:** On its pricing page Zendesk lists **Support Team at $19, Suite Team at $55 and Suite Professional at $115 per agent per month, paid yearly**. Suite Enterprise with Copilot is sold through sales. A monthly option exists but costs more, because the page advertises 20% off for annual billing.

*Checked on Zendesk's pricing page on 16 October 2026. Prices shown are the annual rates; confirm current monthly pricing before you buy.*

## The plans

| Plan | Price (per agent, paid yearly) | Built for |
|---|---|---|
| Support Team | $19/month | Teams that have outgrown a shared inbox |
| Suite Team | $55/month | Teams ready to unify support channels and automate with AI agents |
| Suite Professional | $115/month | Teams optimizing operations with advanced automation (marked Most Popular) |
| Suite Enterprise + Copilot | Talk to sales | Advanced security, governance and the most proactive AI assistant |

## What each tier adds

**Support Team** gives you the basics: an email and ticketing system, ticket routing, prebuilt analytics dashboards, pre-written responses, customer context, and automations and triggers.

**Suite Team** includes the Support Team features and adds AI agents, an AI knowledge base, an AI action builder, omnichannel routing, messaging and live chat, and telephony.

**Suite Professional** adds an AI admin copilot, an AI app builder, AI writing tools, AI quick reports, skills-based routing and an IVR phone tree.

**Suite Enterprise + Copilot** adds intelligent triage, auto assist, generative AI for voice, approval workflows, a sandbox environment and custom agent roles.

## Which one do you need?

- **Email-only support:** Support Team covers ticketing and routing at the lowest price.
- **Chat, messaging and phone in one place:** the jump to Suite Team is where those channels and the AI agents appear, so budget for roughly three times the Support Team price per agent.
- **Phone trees and skills-based routing:** that starts at Suite Professional.
- **Security, governance and sandboxing:** Enterprise, by quote.

A useful sanity check is to multiply the per-agent price by your agent count and by 12. Ten agents on Suite Team at the annual rate is 10 x $55 x 12 = $6,600 a year before any add-ons, which is our arithmetic from the listed price, not a Zendesk quote.

## Alternatives

If you want per-seat pricing with a different AI model, see our guide to [Intercom pricing](/articles/intercom-pricing-helpdesk-seats-and-fin-per-outcome), which bills its AI agent per resolved conversation. [Freshdesk](/tools/freshdesk) is another help desk to compare.

The full review is on our [Zendesk page](/tools/zendesk).

## Sources

- Zendesk pricing page (zendesk.com/pricing), checked 16 October 2026

title: Intercom Pricing: Helpdesk Seats and Fin Priced Per Outcome
excerpt: Intercom charges per seat for the helpdesk and $0.99 per outcome for its Fin AI Agent. Here is how to estimate the bill and whether there is a free plan.
seoTitle: Intercom Pricing: Seats Plus Fin Per Outcome
seoDescription: Intercom helpdesk plans from $19 per seat, Fin AI Agent at $0.99 per outcome, the 14-day free trial and how to estimate a monthly bill.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
Help desk with per-agent tier pricing.

content:
**Quick answer:** Intercom's pricing has two parts: a **per-seat helpdesk fee** (Essential $19, Advanced $85 and Expert $132 per seat per month when paid annually) and **$0.99 per outcome** for its Fin AI Agent. The page offers a **14-day cardless free trial**, and it does not list a permanent free plan.

*Checked on Intercom's pricing page on 16 October 2026. Prices shown are for annual payment; confirm current terms before buying.*

## The helpdesk plans

| Plan | Helpdesk price | Fin AI Agent | Notable inclusions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Essential | $19 per seat/month | $0.99 per outcome | Messenger live chat, shared inbox and ticketing, pre-built reports, public help center, basic automation |
| Advanced | $85 per seat/month | $0.99 per outcome | Everything in Essential plus workflow automation builder, multiple team inboxes, round robin assignment, private and multilingual help center, 20 free Lite seats |
| Expert | $132 per seat/month | $0.99 per outcome | Everything in Advanced plus SSO and identity management, HIPAA support, SLAs, multibrand Messenger and help center, 50 free Lite seats |

The page says paying annually saves up to 35%.

## How Fin is billed

Fin AI Agent costs **$0.99 per outcome** on all plans. Intercom's rules on its page are worth knowing because they limit what you can be charged:

- If Fin cannot answer, fails to take an action, or the customer asks to speak to a human, you pay nothing.
- You are charged at most **one outcome per conversation**, even if Fin takes several actions.
- If a conversation is reopened later, the outcome is refunded.
- Spending limits and alerts are available.

You can also use Fin on top of an existing helpdesk such as Salesforce, HubSpot or Freshdesk, at the same $0.99 per outcome, by contacting sales. Fin Voice is listed at $1.99 per voice outcome through sales.

## A quick estimate

This is our arithmetic from the published prices, not an Intercom quote. A small team with 2 Essential seats and 500 conversations resolved by Fin in a month would pay about:

- Helpdesk: 2 x $19 = $38
- Fin: 500 x $0.99 = $495
- **Total: about $533 a month**

The AI portion scales with how many conversations Fin resolves, so a busy inbox can cost far more in outcomes than in seats. That is the number to model before you commit.

## Is there a free plan?

The pricing page shows a 14-day free trial that does not need a credit card and does not show a permanent free plan. There is also an Early Stage offer for startups that have raised under $10M and have 15 employees or fewer.

## How it compares

If you prefer fixed per-agent tiers, read our [Zendesk pricing guide](/articles/zendesk-pricing-explained-support-team-vs-suite). The full review is on our [Intercom page](/tools/intercom).

## Sources

- Intercom pricing page (intercom.com/pricing), checked 16 October 2026

title: Notion Pricing: Free, Plus, Business or Enterprise?
excerpt: Notion lists Free, Plus at $10, Business at $20 and custom Enterprise pricing. Here is what each includes and when to upgrade.
seoTitle: Notion Pricing: Free, Plus, Business or Enterprise?
seoDescription: Notion plans compared: Free, Plus $10, Business $20 per member a month and Enterprise, with what each adds and how to pick.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
A notes app alternative that stores files locally.

content:
**Quick answer:** Notion lists four plans: **Free ($0), Plus ($10), Business ($20) and Enterprise (custom)**, with Plus and Business priced per member per month. The page offers a yearly option that it says saves up to 20%.

*Checked on Notion's pricing page on 16 October 2026. The page has a monthly/yearly toggle, so confirm which billing mode a price refers to before you buy.*

## The plans

| Plan | Price | Described as |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 per member/month | For individuals to organize personal projects and life |
| Plus | $10 per member/month | For small teams and professionals to work together |
| Business | $20 per member/month (marked Recommended) | For growing businesses to streamline teamwork |
| Enterprise | Custom pricing | For organizations that need scale, control and security |

## What Free includes

Free includes a trial of Notion AI, basic forms, publishing a page to the web, basic sites, Notion Calendar and databases with subtasks, dependencies and custom properties. The page notes that pages and blocks are unlimited for individuals but limited for teams of two or more, so a team that wants to collaborate can try it on Free up to a certain number of blocks before upgrading.

## What Plus adds

Plus includes everything in Free and adds the ability to remove Notion branding from public forms, custom forms, custom sites (custom header, theme, favicon and Google Analytics), unlimited charts, unlimited collaborative blocks, unlimited file uploads (subject to a per-file size limit) and basic connections to tools such as Slack and Google Drive.

## What Business adds

Business includes everything in Plus and is the plan the page frames as the AI workspace. It lists Notion Agent for multi-step tasks, AI meeting notes, enterprise search (beta), SAML single sign-on, granular database permissions, page verification, private teamspaces, domain verification and premium connections such as GitHub and Asana.

## What Enterprise adds

Enterprise includes everything in Business plus zero data retention with LLM providers when using Notion AI, SCIM user provisioning, advanced security controls, an audit log, a customer success manager, DLP and SIEM connections, domain management and advanced connections. It is priced by contacting sales.

Separately, the page lists Custom Agents as free to try, then **$10 per 1,000 monthly Notion credits**.

## How to choose

- **Personal use:** Free is built for it.
- **A small team that needs unlimited blocks and uploads:** Plus.
- **SSO, granular permissions or the AI agent features:** Business.
- **Compliance, SCIM or audit needs:** Enterprise.

A rough budget check is members times price: ten members on Plus at $10 would be $100 a month at that listed rate, before any yearly discount.

If you prefer a local-first notes app, compare [Obsidian](/tools/obsidian). Our full review is on the [Notion page](/tools/notion).

## Sources

- Notion pricing page (notion.com/pricing), checked 16 October 2026

title: Vercel Pricing: Hobby vs Pro and When to Upgrade
excerpt: Vercel's Hobby plan is free and Pro is $20 a month with $20 of included usage. Here is what each includes and what Enterprise adds.
seoTitle: Vercel Pricing: Hobby vs Pro and When to Upgrade
seoDescription: Vercel Hobby is $0 and Pro is $20 a month with included usage credit. What each plan includes, CDN limits and what Enterprise adds.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
A comparable hosting platform to evaluate.
A common backend pairing for Vercel-hosted apps.

content:
**Quick answer:** Vercel's **Hobby plan is $0 a month** for web apps and personal projects, and **Pro is $20 a month** with $20 of included usage credit, team collaboration and a flat-rate CDN. Enterprise is custom priced.

*Checked on Vercel's pricing page on 16 October 2026. All prices are in USD and exclude taxes. Plans and limits can change.*

## The plans

| Plan | Price | Described as |
|---|---|---|
| Hobby | $0/month | The perfect starting place for your web app or personal project |
| Pro | $20/month | Everything you need to build and scale your app |
| Enterprise | Custom | Critical security, performance, observability, platform SLAs and support |

## What Hobby includes

The page lists: import your repo and deploy in seconds, automatic CI/CD, a Web Application Firewall, a global automated CDN, Fluid compute, DDoS mitigation, and traffic and performance insights. The comparison table shows 1M CDN requests a month and 100 GB of Fast Data Transfer a month included on Hobby, and up to 3 custom firewall rules.

## What Pro adds

Pro includes all Hobby features plus:

- **$20 of included usage credit**
- A **flat-rate CDN** with traffic spike protection
- Advanced spend management
- Team collaboration and free viewer seats
- Cold start prevention
- A free custom domain

The comparison table also raises the firewall limits to up to 40 custom rules, and spend management lets you set a limit and get alerts so usage stops before you go over budget.

## What Enterprise adds

Enterprise includes all Pro features plus guest and team access controls, SCIM and directory sync, managed WAF rulesets, multi-region compute and failover, a 99.99% SLA and advanced support.

## When to upgrade

1. **You work with a team.** Team collaboration and viewer seats are Pro features.
2. **You want spend controls.** Advanced spend management is part of Pro.
3. **You need predictable CDN costs.** Pro uses a flat-rate CDN with traffic spike protection.
4. **You have compliance needs.** SCIM, managed WAF rulesets and the 99.99% SLA are Enterprise.

Before relying on Hobby for a commercial project, read Vercel's own terms for the plan, because the pricing page describes Hobby for personal projects and does not spell out commercial-use rules.

A frequent pairing is Vercel for the front end with [Supabase](/tools/supabase) for the database, and our [Supabase pricing guide](/articles/supabase-pricing-free-plan-limits-and-what-pro-adds) explains that side. [Netlify](/tools/netlify) is a comparable host. See the [Vercel page](/tools/vercel) for our review.

## Sources

- Vercel pricing page (vercel.com/pricing), checked 16 October 2026

title: Plausible Analytics Pricing: Is It a Google Analytics Alternative?
excerpt: Plausible is a paid, privacy-focused analytics tool with plans from $9 a month. Here is what each plan includes and how it differs from Google Analytics.
seoTitle: Plausible Analytics Pricing and GA4 Alternative
seoDescription: Plausible Analytics plans from $9 a month: Starter, Growth and Business compared, with the 30-day trial and how it differs from GA4.

tools.note: The tool this guide is about.
The free tool Plausible positions itself against.
Another privacy-focused analytics tool.

content:
**Quick answer:** [Plausible](/tools/plausible-analytics) is a paid, privacy-focused analytics tool. Its pricing section lists **Starter from $9 a month, Growth from $14 and Business from $19** at the lowest pageview tier (up to 10k monthly pageviews), scaling with traffic, plus a 30-day free trial with no credit card.

*Checked on Plausible's homepage pricing section on 16 October 2026. The price shown depends on your monthly pageview tier and the monthly/yearly toggle (yearly shows "2 months free"), so confirm your own tier before buying.*

## The plans

| Plan | From | Sites | Team members | Highlights |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $9/month | One site | Not listed | 3 years of data retention, dashboard, email/Slack reports, Google Analytics import, goals and custom events, saved segments, annotations |
| Growth | $14/month | Up to 3 sites | Up to 3 | Everything in Starter plus team management, shared links, embedded dashboards, shared segments and annotations |
| Business | $19/month | Up to 10 sites | Up to 10 | Everything in Growth plus 5 years of data retention, custom properties, Stats API (600 requests per hour), Data Studio connector, ecommerce revenue attribution, funnels and user journeys |
| Enterprise | Custom | 10+ sites | 10+ | SSO, managed proxy, scheduled raw event exports, priority support |

Prices scale with monthly pageviews, and the page lists tiers from 10k up to 10M+.

## What Plausible says it is

The company describes itself as independent, self-funded and profitable, running since 2018, made and hosted in the EU, with open-source code. Its marketing lists simple metrics, a lightweight script, a privacy focus and no cookie banner.

## How it differs from Google Analytics

The main difference is the business model: Plausible is subscription-funded, while Google Analytics 4 has a free plan. That means a Plausible bill grows with your traffic. Plausible also offers a Google Analytics import on the Starter plan, which helps if you want to keep historical data when switching.

Whether it is a replacement depends on what you use GA4 for. Plausible positions simple, privacy-friendly reporting, so check that the goals, events, funnels and ecommerce attribution you rely on are covered on the plan you would buy. We have not tested feature parity, so run the free trial against your real needs.

## How to choose

- **One site, simple reporting:** Starter.
- **Up to three sites or shared dashboards:** Growth.
- **Funnels, ecommerce attribution or the Stats API:** Business.
- **SSO or a managed proxy:** Enterprise.

See our [Plausible Analytics page](/tools/plausible-analytics) and compare [Google Analytics](/tools/google-analytics) and [Fathom](/tools/fathom-analytics).

seoDescription: Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot compared on price, plans, where each runs and who should choose which, using vendor pricing pages.

tools.note: Agentic coding tool from Anthropic.
AI assistant built into editors and GitHub.

content:
**Quick answer:** Pick [GitHub Copilot](/tools/github-copilot) if you want an assistant inside your editor and on GitHub, with a free tier and a **$10 a month** Pro plan. Pick [Claude Code](/tools/claude-code) if you want an agent that works across your whole codebase and runs commands, which starts at **$17 a month billed annually ($20 monthly)** on Pro and has no free tier.

*Prices come from each vendor's pricing page, checked on 16 October 2026. Both vendors state that usage limits apply and plans can change. We have not benchmarked output quality, so this comparison covers price, plans and where each tool runs.*

## At a glance

| | Claude Code | GitHub Copilot |
|---|---|---|
| Free plan | No | Yes, with limited chat and agent usage |
| Lowest paid plan | Pro: $17/month billed annually, or $20 monthly | Pro: $10/month |
| Higher tiers | Max from $100/month (5x or 20x Pro usage) | Pro+ $39/month, Max $100/month |
| Where it runs | Terminal, IDE extensions, desktop app, browser | Editors and IDEs, CLI, GitHub and GitHub Mobile |
| How limits work | Usage limits on every plan | Monthly GitHub AI Credits |

## How they are positioned

Claude Code's documentation describes an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and integrates with your development tools. Copilot's plans page emphasises chat, agent mode, code review, a cloud agent and a CLI, consuming monthly credits, with support across many editors and on GitHub itself.

There is overlap, because both now offer agent features. The difference you will feel day to day is where you work: Copilot is woven into your editor and your GitHub workflow, while Claude Code is a standalone tool you point at a repository.

## Price in practice

For one developer the cheapest comparison is **Copilot Pro at $10 a month against Claude Code on Pro at $17 a month (annual billing)**. Copilot also has a free plan, so you can try it before paying; Claude Code does not. At the high end both list a $100 a month tier, but they measure usage differently, so compare how much you would actually use rather than the headline price.

## Who should choose which

- **You live in your editor and on GitHub pull requests:** Copilot. Pull request reviews and assigning work to Copilot are paid-plan features.
- **You want to delegate multi-file tasks from the terminal:** Claude Code.
- **You are on a tight budget or want to try first:** Copilot Free.
- **You expect heavy daily agent use:** price out Claude Max against Copilot Pro+ or Max using your own usage.

You do not have to choose permanently. Many developers use an editor assistant for everyday completions and an agent for larger changes, and monthly billing makes it cheap to test both.

For the detail behind each side, read our [Claude Code pricing guide](/articles/claude-code-pricing-which-plan-do-you-need) and our [GitHub Copilot plans guide](/articles/github-copilot-plans-compared-free-pro-pro-plus-max).

- GitHub Copilot plans page (github.com/features/copilot/plans), checked 16 October 2026
- Claude Code documentation overview (docs.claude.com), checked 16 October 2026
